**Resolved:** The reported same-name fallback is closed. In [walk.rs](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs:619), relative `workspace:` specs use only the directory-matched target; a miss now produces the “does not identify an admitted npm workspace member” diagnostic instead of falling back by name. The e2e regression at [native_resolution_e2e_tests.rs](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-cli/tests/native_resolution_e2e_tests.rs:710) sets the relative target outside workspace admission while giving it the same name as an admitted member, and checks for that diagnostic. Alias specs still resolve by their declared target name; directory-relative specs still derive their target name from the target manifest in [npm.rs](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-manifests/src/npm.rs:68). Dependency declaration keys remain preserved for rewrites.

**Remaining finding — Low, confirmed by tracing:** relative workspace member matching can fail when the workspace root is supplied through a symlink. `relative_workspace_target` canonicalizes `root` and returns a path relative to that canonical root ([walk.rs](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs:21)); the subsequent candidate path is also canonicalized, but stripped against the original, potentially symlinked `root` ([walk.rs](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs:604)). Those paths do not share a prefix. A valid admitted relative dependency can therefore be omitted from the graph and reported as unknown, preventing its cascade edge from being followed. I found no symlink-root regression covering this case.
